title: E-Scooters More Dangerous than Motorbikes, Bicycles
paragraphs: E-scooters can be a great way to get around a city. You can hop on one and get from one part of town to another in no time, without having to deal with crowded buses and trains. And unlike cycling, you can do it without even breaking a sweat!
But new findings might make you think twice before using one.

A new study, published in Scientific Reports, looked at over 15,000 people who were taken to hospitals in England and Wales with moderate or serious injuries after e-scooter, motorcycle or bicycle accidents between 2020 and 2022.
Researchers found that injured adult e-scooter riders were 3.5 times more likely to suffer a serious brain injury than motorcyclists, and 1.7 times more likely to do so than cyclists.
They were also about 50% more likely than motorcyclists to suffer injuries to internal organs.

The study, however, is not saying that someone riding an e-scooter is more likely to crash or get hurt. It only looked at the seriousness of the injuries people had when they got taken to the hospital after they'd already had an accident.
So what makes e-scooters so much more dangerous when they have a serious crash?
One possible reason is that very few e-scooter riders wear helmets. In the study, fewer than 6% were wearing one, while that number was 76% for motorcyclists and 45% for cyclists.
Study author David Bodansky also pointed to their small wheels, which can easily get caught in potholes and send riders head-first onto the ground.
So if you're thinking of hopping on an e-scooter for a short ride around town, don't forget that safety comes first!
